actions.description: Mark setup complete and dismiss the wizard. Persists via the same `complete_setup` Tauri command the user-driven 'Finish' button uses. Does NOT save process configs — a programmatic caller has picked none.
actions.label: Complete Setup

actions.description: Open the wizard at a specific step. Values 0-6 correspond to: Tier, Welcome, Projects, Processes, Dev Services, AI Provider, Claude Sessions. NON-DESTRUCTIVE: opening flips in-memory view state only; the persisted `setup_completed` setting is untouched.
actions.label: Jump to Step

components.description: First-launch onboarding wizard. Use 'complete' to dismiss programmatically without driving 7 step interactions. Use 'go-to-step' to jump to a specific step (0-6) — this also OPENS the wizard if it is currently dismissed, which is how you reach first-run surfaces on a runner that auto-bypassed setup (any supervisor temp runner, unless spawned with extra_env: { QONTINUI_TEST_AUTO_LOGIN_EMAIL: "" }).
components.name: Setup Wizard

customActions.description: REFUSED on a pane with no mounted view: there is nothing focusable. Scroll or select the pane so its TerminalInstance mounts, then focus it.
REFUSED on a pane with no mounted view: nothing here can hold focus.

Send key sequences to the terminal by id (no mounted view). Accepts `keys` as a raw string (written verbatim), an array of key names (["Enter"]), or the SDK's descriptor array ([{ key: "c", modifiers: { ctrl: true } }]). Fails with TERMINAL_EXITED when the pane's process is gone.
Write text directly to the PTY by id (no mounted view). Fails with WRITE_TEXT_INVALID when `text` is not a string, and with TERMINAL_EXITED when the pane's process is gone.
Read clipboard and write to the PTY by id (same as Ctrl+V, no mounted view).

Paste literal text to the PTY by id (no mounted view), through the same bracketed-paste-aware path as the mounted pane: the PTY's DEC 2004 state is read from the runner's own VT parser by id. Fails with PASTE_TEXT_INVALID when `text` is not a string.

Read the terminal's scrollback as plain text. With no mounted xterm this comes from the Rust PTY ring rather than the rendered buffer, with escape sequences stripped. Fails with SCROLLBACK_MAX_LINES_INVALID when `maxLines` is not a positive integer.
